review: 1:1 עַל־צְלָב גָּלְגָּלְתָּא — the Arabic keeps both nouns (صَلِيبِ الْجُلْجُثَة), and so does the Hebrew; צְלָב is the glossary's fixed word, and גָּלְגָּלְתָּא stays Aramaic as the place-name rather than being Hebraised to 'the skull place'.
2:1–2 מֵתִים הָיִינוּ כֻּלָּנוּ — Eph 2:1; the Hebrew keeps the plural and the 'all of us', so the rescue is not the rescue of an individual only.
2:3–4 וּבְעַנְוָה עוֹלָה עַל־כֹּל … כָּעֲבָדִים — Phil 2:7–8 (דְּמוּת עֶבֶד); the plural כָּעֲבָדִים keeps the Arabic كَالْعَبِيد, i.e. He lived the life slaves live, not merely 'like a servant'.

3:1–2 the One who gives the thirsty drink thirsted, and vinegar too He drank — John 19:28–29 with Ps 69:22 (בְּצָמְאִי יַשְׁקוּנִי חֹמֶץ); the participle מַשְׁקֶה is kept against the finite 'He gives drink', so the irony stands in one breath.

4:1–4 the seventh word is split exactly where the print splits it (أَبَتَاه / الْكُلَّ أَكْمَلْتُ / أَسْتَوْدِعُ / رُوحِي), and the Hebrew follows John 19:30 (נִשְׁלַם) with Ps 31:6 (בְּיָדְךָ אַפְקִיד רוּחִי), so the last line quotes the psalm Jesus quoted.
6:1–4 is identical to tr0205 6:1–4 in the print and is kept word-for-word identical here.
